name: Flowering of organised Sufism
summary: Sufi tariqas (brotherhoods) organise around founding masters: the Qadiriyya (Abdul Qadir Gilani d.1166), the Rifa'iyya (1183), Suhrawardiyya, Chishtiyya (carried to India), and the Mevlevi order founded around Jalal al-Din Rumi at Konya (1273). Hospices (khanqahs), poetry, and dhikr ritual spread across the Islamic world.

_quarry.structural_significance: Sufi networks become the principal vehicle for Islamic expansion into South Asia, Anatolia, the Balkans, and sub-Saharan Africa over the next four centuries, preceding and outlasting military conquest. Ibn al-Arabi's metaphysical synthesis (d.1240) shapes Islamic mystical philosophy permanently.
